questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'prodigal':
questions.explanation: Prodigal means wasteful, so its opposite is thrifty.

questions.question: Combine into a complex sentence: He is poor. He is honest.
options: He is poor so he is honest.
Though he is poor, he is honest.
questions.explanation: A subordinate clause with though makes it complex, not merely compound.

questions.question: The idiom 'a blessing in disguise' means:
options: a good thing that first seemed bad
questions.explanation: It describes something that looks like misfortune but turns out well.

questions.question: 'The camel is the ship of the desert' is an example of:
questions.explanation: One thing is called another directly, so it is a metaphor.

questions.question: Correct the sentence: Each of the boys have a pen.
options: Each of the boys have a pen.
Each of the boys had have a pen.
Each of the boys has a pen.
Each of the boys are having a pen.
questions.explanation: Each takes a singular verb, so it is has.

questions.question: The word 'stationery' means:
questions.explanation: Stationery with an e means writing materials; stationary with an a means not moving.

questions.question: 'As quiet as a nun' is an example of:
questions.explanation: The comparison uses 'as', which marks a simile.

questions.question: Geoffrey Chaucer's most celebrated work is:
questions.explanation: The Canterbury Tales is Chaucer's masterpiece; the others are by Langland, Malory and Spenser.

questions.question: The protagonist of Mulk Raj Anand's novel 'Untouchable' is:
questions.explanation: Bakha, a young sweeper, is the central figure of Untouchable.

questions.question: The repetition of similar vowel sounds in nearby words is called:
questions.explanation: Assonance is the repetition of vowel sounds; alliteration repeats initial consonants.

questions.question: Walt Whitman's life-long, repeatedly revised poetry collection is:
questions.explanation: Whitman kept enlarging Leaves of Grass across many editions.

questions.question: Shelley's cry 'O World! O Life! O Time!' is an example of:
questions.explanation: The poet directly addresses absent or abstract things, which is apostrophe.

questions.question: T. S. Eliot's poem 'The Waste Land' was first published in which year?
questions.explanation: The Waste Land appeared in 1922, the same year as Joyce's Ulysses.

questions.question: Rearrange into a meaningful sentence: always / truth / the / speak
questions.explanation: The natural imperative order is Always speak the truth.

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelled word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling has one c, two s: Occasion.

questions.question: 'Frailty, thy name is woman' is spoken in which play by Shakespeare?
questions.explanation: Hamlet says it about his mother Gertrude in his first soliloquy.

questions.question: T. S. Eliot famously called which play 'an artistic failure'?
questions.explanation: Eliot made this claim in his essay Hamlet and His Problems.

questions.question: Change into indirect speech: She said, 'I am writing a letter.'
options: She said that she is writing a letter.
She said that she had written a letter.
She said that she was writing a letter.
She said that I was writing a letter.
questions.explanation: Present continuous shifts to past continuous and the pronoun changes to she.

questions.question: The character Shylock appears in which play by Shakespeare?
questions.explanation: Shylock the moneylender belongs to The Merchant of Venice.

questions.question: The title of Faulkner's novel 'The Sound and the Fury' is taken from a speech in which play?
questions.explanation: It comes from Macbeth's 'sound and fury, signifying nothing' speech.

questions.question: The orphan hero named Pip appears in which Dickens novel?
questions.explanation: Pip is the narrator and hero of Great Expectations.

questions.question: Who described Shelley as 'a beautiful and ineffectual angel'?
questions.explanation: The phrase is from Matthew Arnold's essay on Shelley.

questions.question: Pick the correctly spelled word from the options:
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is Separate, with an a in the middle.

questions.question: In Wordsworth's famous lyric 'I wandered lonely as a cloud', the poet sees a host of:
questions.explanation: The poem describes a crowd of golden daffodils beside a lake.

questions.question: 'The pen is mightier than the sword' uses which figure of speech?
questions.explanation: Pen and sword stand for writing and warfare, so the figure is metonymy.

questions.question: 'April is the cruellest month' is the opening line of which poem?
questions.explanation: These words open the first section of Eliot's The Waste Land.

questions.question: The idiom 'to let the cat out of the bag' means:
questions.explanation: It means to disclose a secret, often by accident.

questions.question: The novel 'Middlemarch' was written by:
questions.explanation: Middlemarch is George Eliot's best known novel.

questions.question: Choose the antonym of 'augment':
questions.explanation: Augment means to increase, so diminish is its opposite.

questions.question: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'benevolent':
questions.explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning or kind.

questions.question: In 'Macbeth', who speaks the line 'Will all great Neptune's ocean wash this blood clean from my hand?'
questions.explanation: Macbeth says it after killing Duncan; Lady Macbeth's guilt speech is the later sleepwalking scene.

questions.question: The expression 'all the perfumes of Arabia' in Macbeth is an example of:
questions.explanation: It is deliberate exaggeration, hence hyperbole.

questions.question: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said, 'The earth moves round the sun.'
options: The teacher said that the earth is moving round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth moved round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth had moved round the sun.
The teacher said that the earth moves round the sun.
questions.explanation: A universal truth keeps the present tense even after a past reporting verb.

questions.question: Which of the following is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is Definitely.

questions.question: Fill in the correct tense: By next year, he ____ his degree.
questions.explanation: An action finished before a future time takes the future perfect will have completed.

questions.question: Rearrange into a meaningful sentence: a / is / he / teacher / good
questions.explanation: The subject-verb-object order gives He is a good teacher.

questions.question: 'And miles to go before I sleep' is the repeated closing line of which Frost poem?
options: Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening
questions.explanation: The line is repeated at the close of Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening.

questions.question: The adjective formed from the noun 'danger' is:
questions.explanation: The correct adjective is dangerous.

questions.question: A mock-epic treats a trivial subject in the lofty style of:
questions.explanation: A mock-epic applies grand epic style to a trivial theme for comic effect.

questions.question: Arthur Miller's play 'The Crucible' dramatizes which historical episode?
questions.explanation: The Crucible retells the 1692 Salem witch trials as political allegory.

questions.question: The age dominated by Wordsworth, Coleridge, Shelley and Keats is known as the:
questions.explanation: These four are central poets of the Romantic Period.

questions.question: Nissim Ezekiel is often regarded as the father of modern:
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is widely called a father of modern Indian English poetry.

questions.question: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'ephemeral':
questions.explanation: Ephemeral means lasting a very short time.

questions.question: 'A thing of beauty is a joy for ever' is the opening line of which poem by Keats?
questions.explanation: This line opens Keats's long poem Endymion.

questions.question: A word that means the exact opposite of another word is a/an:
questions.explanation: Words of opposite meaning are antonyms.

questions.question: The imaginary regional setting of Thomas Hardy's novels is called:
questions.explanation: Hardy set his novels in the semi-fictional region of Wessex.

questions.question: Toni Morrison was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in:
questions.explanation: Toni Morrison won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1993.

questions.question: In Hemingway's 'The Old Man and the Sea', the old fisherman is named:
questions.explanation: Santiago is the old Cuban fisherman at the centre of the novella.

questions.question: Who wrote the comedy 'Twelfth Night'?
questions.explanation: Twelfth Night is a comedy by Shakespeare; the others are different Elizabethan or Jacobean dramatists.

questions.question: Dickens's novel 'A Tale of Two Cities' is set in London and which other city?
questions.explanation: The two cities are London and Paris during the French Revolution.

questions.question: Toni Morrison's novel about Sethe and the legacy of slavery is:
questions.explanation: Beloved centres on Sethe, a formerly enslaved mother.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: He has been living here since 2010.
questions.explanation: A state continuing from a past point needs the present perfect continuous with since.

questions.question: The noun formed from the verb 'abound' is:
questions.explanation: The noun is abundance; abundant is the adjective.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: He is good ____ mathematics.
questions.explanation: We say good at a subject or skill.

questions.question: Choose the word nearest in meaning to 'candid':
questions.explanation: Candid means open and frank.

questions.question: Among the Romantics, who is especially called the poet of beauty and sensuousness?
questions.explanation: Keats is traditionally called the poet of beauty for his rich sensuous imagery.

questions.question: The novel 'Tess of the d'Urbervilles' was written by:
questions.explanation: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is one of Hardy's major tragic novels.

questions.question: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
questions.explanation: A direct question begins with a capital and ends with a question mark.

questions.question: 'Ode to the West Wind' ends with which famous line?
options: Ring out the old, ring in the new
If Winter comes, can Spring be far behind?
questions.explanation: That hopeful closing line is Shelley's; the others belong to Keats, Shelley's Skylark and Tennyson.

questions.question: Change into the passive voice: They built this house in 1990.
options: This house has been built in 1990.
questions.explanation: Past simple active becomes was plus past participle built in the passive.

questions.question: The Metaphysical poets, such as Donne, belong chiefly to which century?
questions.explanation: Metaphysical poetry flourished in the seventeenth century.

questions.question: Arthur Miller's tragedy about the travelling salesman Willy Loman is:
questions.explanation: Willy Loman is the hero of Death of a Salesman.

questions.question: 'George Eliot' was the pen name of:
questions.explanation: The novelist George Eliot was really Mary Ann Evans.

questions.question: In which poem does Keats write 'Beauty is truth, truth beauty'?
questions.explanation: The lines close Keats's Ode on a Grecian Urn.

questions.question: Change into indirect speech: He said, 'What a beautiful scene!'
options: He exclaimed that it was a very beautiful scene.
He said that what a beautiful scene.
He exclaimed what a beautiful scene.
He asked what a beautiful scene it was.
questions.explanation: Exclamatory sentences become statements introduced by exclaimed that.

questions.question: Geoffrey Chaucer is traditionally called the father of English:
questions.explanation: Chaucer is honoured as the father of English poetry.

questions.question: The idiom 'to burn the midnight oil' means:
options: to work late into the night
questions.explanation: It means to study or work until late at night.

questions.question: Wordsworth and Coleridge jointly published which volume in 1798?
questions.explanation: Lyrical Ballads, published in 1798, is a landmark of English Romanticism.

questions.question: Rearrange into a meaningful sentence: to / likes / she / read / books
questions.explanation: The correct order is She likes to read books.

questions.question: 'The old order changeth, yielding place to new' is a line from Tennyson's:
questions.explanation: The line comes from Tennyson's Morte d'Arthur, later part of the Idylls of the King.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a tragedy by Shakespeare?
questions.explanation: The Tempest is a romance or comedy; Othello, King Lear and Macbeth are tragedies.

questions.question: Charles Lamb wrote his essays under which pen name?
questions.explanation: Lamb published as Elia; Boz was Dickens, Saki was H. H. Munro.

questions.question: A government by a small privileged group is called:
questions.explanation: Rule by a few is an oligarchy.

questions.question: 'Good fences make good neighbours' is a line from which Robert Frost poem?
questions.explanation: The proverb is quoted by the neighbour in Mending Wall.

questions.question: One who can speak many languages is called a:
questions.explanation: A polyglot knows and uses several languages.

questions.question: Shakespeare was born in which English town?
questions.explanation: Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564.

questions.question: Shelley's elegy on the death of John Keats is titled:
questions.explanation: Adonais is Shelley's elegy for Keats; Lycidas is Milton's, Thyrsis is Arnold's, In Memoriam is Tennyson's.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: One of my friends ____ a doctor.
questions.explanation: The subject is one, which is singular, so the verb is is.

questions.question: Fill in the correct form: She ____ to school every day.
questions.explanation: A habitual action with a third person singular subject takes goes.

questions.question: Which prefix added to 'polite' forms its opposite?
questions.explanation: The opposite of polite is impolite.

questions.question: In literary history the 'Renaissance' chiefly means the revival of:
questions.explanation: The Renaissance revived classical Greek and Latin learning.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: The horse jumped ____ the fence.
questions.explanation: Over expresses movement across and above the fence.

questions.question: The idea that 'poetry is a criticism of life' was put forward by:
questions.explanation: This definition of poetry is Matthew Arnold's.

questions.question: A Shakespearean sonnet consists of how many lines?
questions.explanation: Every sonnet, Shakespearean included, has fourteen lines.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a work by Charles Lamb?
questions.explanation: The Spectator was by Addison and Steele; the rest are Lamb's.

questions.question: Who called Wordsworth's poetic self the 'egotistical sublime'?
questions.explanation: Keats used the phrase in a letter contrasting Wordsworth with his own ideal of negative capability.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: She has been ill ____ Monday.
questions.explanation: Since is used with a point of time such as Monday.

questions.question: Tennyson's long elegy written for Arthur Henry Hallam is:
questions.explanation: In Memoriam A. H. H. is Tennyson's elegy for his friend Arthur Hallam.

questions.question: Kamala Das's autobiography is titled:
questions.explanation: My Story is Kamala Das's autobiography; the others are poetry collections.

questions.question: Who wrote the poem 'Ode to the West Wind'?
questions.explanation: Ode to the West Wind is one of Shelley's best known odes.
